failure_observed: Readers of skill-written papers reconstruct the authors' own limitations (Q11), motivation (Q2) and design rationale (Q5) worse than readers of plain papers: author-stated limitations are replaced by writer-derived caveats presented in the authors' voice, and author rationale is compressed into the writer's spine framing. The skill as executed also differs from the skill as designed: section contracts and attribution-relevant rules sit in files no run opened, the validator and linter were never run, and all gates were self-certified. Two of six skill papers exceeded the 4,500-word limit (0/6 plain).

metrics.F2_note: F2 (3 paired projects) shows no Q2/Q5 loss and Q11 0.756 vs 0.778; the S2 effect is reader-dependent
metrics.S3_runs_self_certifying_all_gates: 4/4 runs with a readable state.json (1 run had malformed state.json)

secondary_causes: conflicting_rules: LIMITATIONS 'must not: generic limitations' + LIMITATION_MISSING 'draft from the claim graph' pushed out broad author limitations
components.summary: New evidence kind rationale_stated; required limitation.origin (author_stated | writer_derived); optional claim.origin and claim.rationale (motivation | design_choice). Validator: every live limitation_noted item is carried by an author_stated limitation, author_stated limitations must cite limitation_noted evidence, every rationale_stated item is carried by an author_stated rationale claim. Lint on assembled drafts: author_stated limitations and rationale claims must be tagged (ERROR), writer-derived caveats mixed into the authors' limitations and rationale placed outside Introduction/Method (WARN). Limitations contract: all author-stated limitations first, attributed; writer-derived caveats after, in an 'Additional caveats' paragraph; broad author limitations attach to the central claim instead of being dropped as generic.

secondary_causes: wrong_placement: load-bearing rules only in unread secondary files
components.summary: Gates G1/G3/G5 become executable: a 'passed' gate needs a tool report under .rcs/audits/gates/ (validate_artifacts --out, lint_draft --out) with 0 errors and matching SHA-256 of the checked inputs; validate_artifacts.py .rcs flags any other 'passed' gate as SELF_CERTIFIED_GATE and flags malformed state.json. SKILL.md now inlines the attribution rules, a one-table section-contract summary, the claim_type/confidence enums, and the gate commands; the 'tools are optional' wording is removed ('unverified' replaces 'passed' when tools cannot run).

length_limit_words in state.json (or venue words_main); lint counts main-text words excluding references/appendix/supplement and raises S4-over-length (WARN in draft, ERROR with --final); G5 fails if the final lint report is over the limit. Step 21 procedure: relocate SUPPLEMENTARY content, never cut claims, negative results, author-stated limitations, or rationale. Step 8 architecture gains a planned-words column (target <= 90% of the limit).

change.summary: Three independently testable parts (see components): (1) attribution-preserving limitation and rationale fields, checks and section contract; (2) executable gates plus inlining of never-read load-bearing rules into SKILL.md; (3) a length gate with a relocation-not-deletion procedure. No hard rule relaxed; no existing test changed except for path resolution in the copied test_tools.py (the candidate keeps tools/ beside SKILL.md).

expected_improvement: Primary: Q11 recall (F1 reader) recovers toward the plain baseline (skill 0.536 vs plain 0.749); expected +0.10 to +0.20 absolute, because author-stated limitations can no longer silently disappear from claim map or assembled draft. Q2/Q5 recall (F1): expected +0.05 to +0.10 each, smaller and less certain, because rationale coverage depends on the extractor recording rationale_stated items (not machine-checkable against the source). DR should not rise (writer caveats are now labelled rather than attributed to authors). S3: validator/lint invocations > 0 in every run, schema errors per run from 141-227 toward 0, no 'passed' gate without a report. S4: 0 papers over the limit.
possible_regressions: More words: attributed author limitations plus a labelled 'Additional caveats' paragraph lengthen Limitations; the length gate counteracts but may push secondary results to the appendix (possible small Q7/Q9 loss).
SKILL.md grows from ~1,170 to ~1,880 words; more instruction text may dilute attention on other rules.
The 'Additional caveats' label may read as unusual in a venue paper; readers may discount writer-derived caveats that are in fact important (Q9/Q11 nuggets that are writer-derived).
Extractor may over-record rationale_stated items (every 'because' in notes), forcing low-value rationale claims into the Introduction/Method and adding words.
Executable gates add tool-run cost and may stall runs where Python is unavailable (gates become 'unverified' instead of 'passed').
S1-caveat-attribution (WARN) fires on every v0.1.0-style text that mixes author and writer limitations in one paragraph, including A_clean.md; it is a warning only, but adds lint noise.
The attribution checks rely on {L###}/{C###} tags; drafts written without tags or in --final mode bypass the draft-side check (the claim-map check and claim-invariance still apply).
Brittle hash-based staleness: harmless re-saves (whitespace) of artifacts after G1 produce a WARN; after G5 they block until the validator is re-run.
